title: A tuning permission is not the selected kernel configuration
applies_when: A configuration-validation proposal interprets enable/allow flags or a planner's coarse cost prediction as the final execution path, especially when a separate knobs resolver or launch plan chooses actual policy. For FlashInfer MegaMoeConfig, trace enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce, combine_dtype and resolved in_kernel_fc2_reduce; for Cake sampling, distinguish _launch_is_two_kernels from _launch_plan, vocabulary and one_launch.
lesson: Trace permission, resolved knobs and the consuming validator separately before adding an earlier rejection. FlashInfer NVFP4 MegaMoE allows enable_in_kernel_fc2_reduce=True while its default selector turns in_kernel_fc2_reduce off for mxfp8/nvfp4 combine wires and selects reuse_dispatch_warps. A constructor regression demanding rejection conflates permission with selection and can reject an existing permitted-but-unselected configuration. Test that control alongside explicitly incompatible selected knobs; inspect where the latter are already rejected. Likewise, Cake sampling's architecture-only two-kernel prediction feeds cost ranking, but the final _launch_plan rechecks _fuse_block_tail with vocabulary and capability. Its one_launch output controls whether stage 2/3 executes. A missing vocabulary argument in the cost predictor alone does not prove the final launch omits stage 2/3. Read the final plan and consumer before changing execution.
avoid_when: An enable flag can be a mandatory execution choice in another API; establish its contract rather than applying this distinction universally. Explicit selected knobs can still be invalid. These pinned sources establish a default-selection counterexample, not all knob combinations, native kernel correctness, distributed reachability or performance. A coarse cost model can still rank variants poorly even when final execution is correct; that needs matched timing rather than a missing-launch assertion. Inconsistent comments may warrant clarification without changing accepted inputs.

evidence.note: The outer config distinguishes permission from knobs that may disable the path. Its wire-format comment alone does not establish that every permitted session selects in-kernel reduction.
The actual default selector forces the selected reduction off for quantized combine wires, even when the caller granted permission.
The lower-level config rejects incompatible selected reduction, wire format and top-k policies before kernel construction. This is source evidence, not a native GPU qualification.

Final _launch_plan passes vocab and capability to _fuse_block_tail, unlike the coarse cost-ranking predicate. This refutes the no-reachable-vocabulary-consumer premise; it does not validate cost-model performance.

The original pure host policy rejects whole-CTA tail for capability (10,3) above vocab 196608. Source-isolated policy controls using the exact registered manifest check the boundary and a bound-removal counterexample; no CUDA or full package execution.
The actual pipeline returns after stage 1 only when plan.one_launch is true; otherwise it calls sparse_topp_sample. Inspecting a planner estimate alone misses this consumer.
